heading: What the world model predicted and what happened
intro: In these tasks a round pusher pushes a block onto a marked goal pose without grasping it. Each of the 17 programs the Code-as-Policies (CaP) agent wrote was run for 200 episodes inside the world model and 50 in the environment. Select a program to see its results, and click any episode mark to replay that episode. Try v5 (the version the agent submitted, 20% in the world model, 16% in the environment) and then v4 (98%, 96%).
world_sub: 200 episodes, 276 lines of Python fitted from a few real trials
real_sub: 50 episodes in the simulator standing in for the real system
hint_marks: Select any mark to replay that episode
outcome_fail: Not solved within the 30 s limit
anim_caption: The outline is the goal pose. An episode succeeds when the block covers more than 95% of the outline within 300 steps. The two sides start from different states because the world model draws its own start positions.
chart_x: Success rate in the world model
chart_legend_all: One point per program (200 world-model, 50 real episodes)
note_recorded: The panel replays recorded runs. Nothing is computed in the browser or on a server.
note_scope: Only the two pushing tasks are shown here. The other six tasks are in the article below and in the repository.

card_body:
An interactive companion to [World Models as Unit Tests](https://dongzhezheng.github.io/world-models-as-unit-tests/). Browse the recorded runs of 17 pushing programs inside the world model and in the environment, with per-episode replay. Code and full results are in the [repository](https://github.com/DongzheZheng/world-models-as-unit-tests).

The programs replayed here are [Code as Policies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07753) programs, and the CaP agent is modelled on [ASPIRE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00272). The note draws on earlier work that writes world models as code: [Code World Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15383), [WorldCoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12275), [CWM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02387), [Code as Worlds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27549) and [Code World Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25927).
